entry_points.text: Release offers a work-list drainer, task-work wrapper, full flush, and sync helpers tearing down at last reference. Sysfs multiplexes name-to-index, protected indexed-name copy and count. Init creates a permanent proc filesystems entry for the cached display, with build-dependent single-entry creation.

Inode binding picks cgroup-aware or default targets exactly once. Offline cleanup migrates dirty inodes toward ancestors or device default. Targeted flush queues a self-releasing cyclic request without creating contexts, reporting absence or exhaustion. Init makes the switch workqueue; background start only wakes the flusher; one predicate spots the shared block-device superblock.

exports.text: igrab holds a possibly-expiring inode or returns null once freeing starts. Filesystem lookup strips dot suffixes, loads on demand, pins the module under read protection, and rejects unsupported subtypes. Shared superblock try-lock succeeds only for born, rooted, live instances.

Sysctl mkdir walks slash paths with usage counts; unregister reconciles peers with diagnostics. Parameter parsing layers lexical lookup, sb flags, security, filesystem handlers and source fallback; monolithic blobs split per separator; contexts offer reconfigure, submount and duplication.

Helpers allocate unaccounted empty or pseudo files, the latter with notifications off and balanced lifetime on failure. Dissolution detaches flagged mounts at last fput. Poll release fast-skips when unlinked; close notifies by write access. Boot enumeration copies block-device filesystem names.

Close cleanup removes open-file-description locks, flock locks, then leases. Flock removal builds an unlock bound to the closing file as file and owner with caller identity, flock type and unbounded extent, using driver handling when present.

Writeback activation offers a workqueue drain handler, a once-per-dirty dontcache kick with held reference, a global walk waking all devices under read protection, and a per-superblock kick gated on immediate shared hold.

hazards.text: Sync waits drop the inode lock while sleeping and recheck the flag. Pseudo allocation balances lifetime on late failure. Lock exhaustion fails acquisition except plain unlock; switch needs shared protection against superblock sync. Missing peers, directory failures and leaked locks only log and continue.

Vanished inodes across sleeps need restart; hold contention needs tail return; deferred entries need sleep; lost wakeups need re-arm; plugs flush before schedule. Log allocation failure uses a static marker; duplicate sources, missing keys, non-string sources and malformed monolithic input fail cleanly.

invariants.text: Table validation requires names and handlers, data plus length for value handlers with element-width checks for uint, byte and bool forms, byte-range bounds, and read-write-only permission bits; diagnostics log path, name and reason and accumulate invalid-argument status.

Close verification warns when any lock still references the file. Same-open-file flock entries never conflict. Anonymous-root needs a valid anonymous namespace with matching root. Context logging uses a power-of-two ring, discarding oldest when full.

Proc display prefers the cached string, regenerating with validation and deferred free of the predecessor, else iterating directly. Sequence append copies only when the total stays strictly below capacity, otherwise records overflow with no partial copy.

Per-sb scans walk the IO tail, returning foreign, new or freeing entries and deferring or sleeping on busy ones, with clamped chunk budgets. Cross-sb draining uses nonblocking holds with tail return on contention. It budgets pages, prefers explicit over background work, and probes full, dontcache, periodic and background triggers in order.

Dirtytime wake walks all devices and re-arms only when enabled, with an interval handler that schedules or cancels. Expiry drains aged tails and regroups by superblock. Dispatch merges deferred work and pulls expired dirty and timestamp entries, the latter on shorter deadlines except during full sync.

Superblock writeback membership is idempotent. Post-writeback disposition separates freeing, skipped, residual-dirty, metadata-only, timestamp-only and clean outcomes. Full or tagged passes use unbounded budgets, others bandwidth shares. Switch batches walk from the aged end; in-flight count is atomic with a dedicated workqueue; trace points live here.

locks.text: Sysctl, flock, lease and close checks use global and file-wide guards with blocked-waiter spin protection. Filesystem reads are read-side guarded, cache publication spin-guarded. Superblock membership is interrupt-guarded; queue prep needs the list lock held. Switch transfer nests inode with page-cache protection; batch migration orders list locks by address.

Queue mutation uses the list lock with inode nesting, dropped across completion sleeps. Explicit work is interrupt-guarded; device walks are read-side. Per-sb draining holds shared superblock locks; duplicated contexts get a fresh user mutex; dontcache marking is atomic with a held reference.

state_machines.text: Opened-file teardown orders notify, poll detach, unlock, security, async, driver, device, operations, owner, access, dentry and mount release with dissolution, then frees; unopened files free directly. Flock completes same-file same-type immediately, replaces on type change, queues sleeping conflicts and fails non-sleeping ones, installing copies when clear.

Ownership transfer moves accounting and membership, refreshes dirty time and marks completion, skipping freeing inodes. Switch work drains batches after a grace period and wakes the new target when anything moved. Dispatch drains explicit requests under running state, then probes full, dontcache, periodic and background triggers in order.

structs.text: Control directories pack directory, node, entry and name together. The filesystem cache holds a deferred-free header with generation, length and text. Writeback requests combine budget, target, sync mode, reason, completion and behavior bits; switch batches add a null-terminated inode set. Filesystem contexts aggregate flags, source, ops, namespaces, credentials, log ring and mutex.

Sysfs selectors are 1 index, 2 name, 3 count. Proc lines use optional nodev, tab, name, newline; boot names are consecutive terminated strings. Mount names map dirsync, lazytime, mand, ro, sync to set bits with async, nolazytime, nomand, rw clearing. Sysctl entries allow only read-write bits; control dirs are read-execute; dirtytime control is dirtytime_expire_seconds mode 0644 lower-bound zero. Sync modes are WB_SYNC_NONE and WB_SYNC_ALL; reasons cover background, periodic, dontcache, forker; params are flag or string; errors use ENOPARAM, EINVAL, ENOMEM, EOPNOTSUPP; log prefix derives from the module name.

Lazy timestamp expiry is 43200 seconds. Foreign detection uses 8192 units per second, one-eighth averaging, cutoff divisor eight, two-second period, sixteen history slots per inode with threshold eight and max run five, and at most 1024 concurrent foreign entries. Switch contexts fit about one kilobyte after header.
